comparator.name: Organization and Management Studies (Organisatie- en Managementwetenschappen)
comparator.sourceNotes: The official 2026–27 curriculum accounts for exactly 180 ECTS: 60 compulsory ECTS in year 1, 60 compulsory ECTS in year 2, and year 3 with 42 compulsory ECTS plus 18 ECTS of genuine exchange or minor space. Zero-credit GROW development is excluded. The complete 12-ECTS organisational-research project and 12-ECTS thesis remain explicit, and no content is invented for the open choice space.

components.name: Vrijekeuzeruimte: exchange or minor
components.note: Genuine 18-ECTS open choice space; no elective content is invented.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest alternative owns organisation theory, sociology, psychology, strategy, collaboration, change, decision-making and public/private management. Innovation and entrepreneurship form one independently coherent direct-interest direction and yield a substantively distinct responsible-change curriculum. All other generator-eligible rows are substantively covered by the closest concept; no third generator-backed direction remains, so production stops at two.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Leadership Communication supports organisational advice and intervention through evidence-based leadership communication.
Social Psychology directly addresses how people’s thought and behaviour are shaped by others and groups.
Introduction to Sociology directly supports Tilburg’s introductory sociology component.
Negotiation & Strategic Thinking directly addresses strategic organisational decision-making.
Psychology of Organizations & Leadership directly addresses organisational behaviour, motivation, culture and decision-making.
Advanced social theory provides a social-scientific framework for institutions and organisations, while remaining broader than Tilburg Organization Theory.
Leadership & Diversity Management addresses inclusive leadership and organisational development.

notes.text: Tilburg prescribes a dense organisation-science sequence spanning organisational sociology and psychology, strategy, methods, networks, development, intervention, a 12-ECTS organisational-research project and a 12-ECTS thesis. UCR can build coherent organisational and responsible-innovation pathways, but it does not reproduce the dedicated labour-law component, the complete methods sequence or the two compulsory research projects; the 18-ECTS free-choice space is preserved as open curriculum.
The Tilburg programme is Dutch-taught, whereas UCR is English-taught. This comparison assesses academic content and structure rather than language of instruction.
